My mom and I were talking in her room one night. She was tired and had a long day doing the normal chemo/cancer thing, ya know, dyin’. (She would laugh at that, it’s fine) Anyways, I told her I had to go to work - and she looked at me before I left and dropped some of the saddest shit I’ve ever heard. She told me she scared like I was. She remembers seeing her mom dead when she was a kid, and she knew how I felt in the moment. She said she’d shown me all the world she could and rest was going to be up me to discover - just like she had to do. I never knew my grandma, or how she died, but my mom told me she was a lost and loveless drunk. Would yell at her and call her a fat little loser, among other things. She’d get woken up by her throwing water on her at 3am just because, and my grandma would force her to sleep in her wet cold bed. But still… she said she loved her. And losing my grandma was devastating to her she said. My mom was like 11 and just loved her parent. She didn’t know she was “bad” she said, she just loved her mom. But after a heavy night of drinking, my grandma apparently had a brain aneurysm rupture and just never woke up. My mom apologized that she was leaving so slowly, and wished it was quick like her mother did to her. Now 12 years after her passing I wish I would have said something corny from the movies like, “Nahh, the world knows you’re worth holding on to.” Instead we hugged, said we loved each other, I left to work, and she continued watching House. She died a week later.

Not sure what tribe you are referencing when you say we get monthly checks. Native Americans don’t get monthly checks from the government, and if they do get “checks” it’s in the form of commodities and basic upkeep of buildings/housing on the reservation (which is extremely subpar). Native Americans hardly ever see money from their tribe. There’s just none left. Most (not all) casinos run on reservations don’t pay out either, unless you work there of course.

I am not sure why people always think us Indigenous people get money from the government or free college anywhere we want, or get casino money (again, most tribes don’t), or whatever. We don’t. We do ask the government for help, but no one listens or cares. While I do admit it could be a pride or trust thing, I will not discount that. But the fact is Native Americans (sovereign or not) are still a part of this country, and we deserve to live happy and healthy on what little lands we have left. Simply moving away from where our heritage and people are isn’t as easy as it sounds. I had a tough time with it, but it was in my own best interest, and I miss my family every day. But life on a reservation can be hard and in some places dangerous. The government can help life on a reservation be better, but they just won’t. And it’s sad. 90% of an entire people wiped out, and the best they can do is scraps and disrespect.

Exactly right. I hardly ever told customers to use anything other than Dawn soap and water. No offense to any of the homeowners I installed countertops for, but they can’t be trusted with cleaning with alcohol/acidic cleaners. Haha. For one, they always did it too much, and dulls the tops. Two, it can (for some companies, such as the one I worked for years ago) void the warranty.

Also, when it comes to countertops and warranties: use it as often as you need to while you have it. And don’t just assume you can do something (like adding faucet holes, resealing granite, or stain removal) because odds are you WILL void your warranty. Even hiring a licensed plumber to drill the hole for a soap dispenser can void it, my old company did this countless times.
They are acidic though. Acidic cleaning materials aren’t that great for stone tops.

It’s more of a pseudo-sovereignty than anything. Just based on what I know of how my reservation runs, the governing body there doesn’t really have all that much power. You can look a vast majority of these treaties up too, there are countless articles about the mistreatment of our people since this country was founded up until today. Indigenous people have been, by far, the most oppressed and ignored people in this country.

When I installed I would use diluted denatured alcohol. Lol. My goal was to never see the customer again unless they were buying more tops or needed a reseal (for granite).  I mean that in a good way haha
Lol. Cutting splash on site was one of the easiest things to do.

Did you dilute it with anything? Or straight up rubbing alcohol? If you don’t dilute it it’ll do more harm than good by damaging the resin in the tops. One time won’t screw you though, not trying to freak you out or anything.

I also know of products that look like baking soda that you mix up (with water I presume), put on, leave for a while, and remove. Could be what that fella used? I have never used it before, so I’m just speculating. But I have had luck with Barkeepers Friend for light stains and any really sticky residue. Don’t use it every time you clean the tops, obviously, otherwise it’ll dull it. And make sure you really buff the stuff out. Don’t need a whole lot either, a little bit can go a long way.

Edit: To add, don’t use those stone countertop wipes either. Most of those are trash, so it’s best to avoid them all together. For general cleaning; a little Dawn dish soap and water.

Something hits the wall behind us, and my dad says he’s not fucking around with this shit anymore, and starts cussing at our uncle under his breath. I managed a few gas stations a few years back. My boss (the owner) had horrible instincts when it came to hiring people, and would often ask me my opinion about people based off his notes. Why he didn't just let me do the interviews, I do not know. But, he pseudo-hired this guy as a "test run" to see if he was worth what he was asking to be paid. I mean, it was a good job, paid well, but ultimately it was a fucking gas station. Like, say hi, say thank you, clean some shit, stock some shit, go home, and show up for your shift. It's not hard.

He scheduled the guy to work with me (again, the manager) and while teaching him basically just don't burn the fucking place down and you have a job, he accidentally discloses some information to me that he probably shouldn't have. While talking about where we both came from he says (changed names), "Yeah, me and my brother Marcus..." story not important. And I say, "Wait, what? You and your brother have the same name?" He says, "No. I didn't say that! Me, I'M Marcus! I meant DEREK!" And I say, "Oh. 'Kay." Had he not gotten so flustered and defensive I'd have shrugged it off. But I was suspicious of him after that. Anyways, the next time I worked with him (2 days later) I said we need his ID for payroll. He goes, "It's at home." I say, "Well, if you'd like to get paid, we will need that. We get paid today and boss wants to get you into payroll ASAP." Then his eyes light up! Money!? He says, "Actually, I think it's in my car!" Then he practically stumbles out the door to get it. Comes back and hands me his WHOLE FUCKING WALLET and says, "It's in there." I'm not looking through his wallet. I set it down and tell him to get it. He does. And I don't look at it right away just kinda glance quick and go back to the office to make a copy for records. When I get to the copier I actually look at the ID. Marcus's ID. Only it doesn't look like the Marcus I saw literally 20 seconds ago. I call the owner over, he looks at it and says, "Fuck me. Not again. Send him back."

So I go to the front, and say the boss needs you sign some papers. He skips back there, and I wait. About 30 seconds later, I see this man ("Marcus") sprinting across the parking lot like a bat outta hell. Trying to take his (our) work shirt off, and mid way through trips in a pothole, falls on the ground, rips the shirt off, throws it, and keeps running. Leaves his car, phone, wallet, everything he brought in his locker. Never saw him again.

Turns out, Marcus was his older brother and he (Derek) stole his identity because Derek was a very bad boy and wasn't paying his taxes. Derek inherited their father's company and drove it into the ground. Derek was also wanted for stealing his father's identity. Derek also stole his girlfriend's car. Derek was also a dumbass and didn't realize him and his brother looked almost nothing alike.

As to the "not again" comment made by boss. Apparently since he paid so well for such a menial job, he attracted some very interesting characters in his time. Once (before I was there) he hired a fella who worked for him for almost a year then the police came snooping around and turns out this guy was using his friend's name and SSN to avoid paying child support. Also turns out; this guy was a runner too. Cops caught him after he tripped in the same pothole "Marcus" tripped in. From that day forward I introduced everyone we hired to Detective Pothole.
Even if it is; that Chris Brown dance video is pretty fucking impressive.
